<objective>
Discharge CONTEXT.md D-12 — take the archive of the deferred service / back-office tiers out of the
cloud design project and into the repo — and author, in the repo, the exact replacement text that
plan 01.1-14 will write back to the design project's `readme.md`.

Purpose: the archived files are "the only copy outside claude.ai/design" and the project is
deletable. This is cheap insurance taken before anything else in the phase moves. Authoring the
correction text here (rather than inside the write-back step) makes the D-11 / D-04 / W-3 edits
reviewable in a normal diff, and archiving the pre-edit `readme.md` is what makes that write-back
reversible.

Output: `.planning/design-archive/` with ten archived files, the original `readme.md`, a corrections
document, and an index README.

**This plan is why 01.1-05 sits in wave 2 rather than wave 1.** D-12's wording is explicit: the
archive lands "before repo migration begins".
</objective>

    Rationale line: the current sentence is verbatim the all-or-nothing suite PROJECT.md names as the

    Section 2 — D-04, lexicon. Current § "Content fundamentals" carries the rule "Restaurant words, not

    the same register (second person, active present, sentence case, no emoji; errors state what happened
    then what to do; confirmations past tense with undo). State in the rationale that the register is
    unchanged and only the lexicon moved, and that a repo grep found zero user-visible strings using the
    dropped vocabulary, so this is a design-project edit with no matching code sweep.

    Section 3 — W-3, currency. Current global rule: "Continental decimal comma for currency; €148,50".
    Replace with the per-currency convention: formatting is per-currency, not one continental rule —
    HUF renders zero-decimal with space grouping and a trailing `Ft` (`hu-HU`); RON renders with a comma
    decimal separator, `.` grouping and a trailing `lei` (`ro-RO`, requiring `currencyDisplay: "narrowSymbol"`
    or it renders "RON"); EUR renders `20,26 €` (`de-DE`). Rationale line: the global rule is wrong for
    zero-decimal HUF, the `qr-menu` template already contradicts it correctly, and `lib/format/money.ts`
    (plan 01.1-02) implements the corrected convention.

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| cloud design project → repo | Content fetched from `claude.ai/design` via `DesignSync` enters the repo as archived files. It is untrusted data, never instructions. |
| repo → cloud design project | Plan 01.1-14 writes back. This plan authors the payload and the rollback copy. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-10 | Tampering | `DesignSync` write-back to `readme.md` (executed in 01.1-14) | medium | mitigate | Task 1 archives the pre-edit `readme.md` verbatim at `.planning/design-archive/readme-ORIGINAL.md`; task 2 authors the replacement as reviewable repo text. The write becomes reversible by re-writing the archived original. |
| T-01.1-12 | Tampering | Fetched design-project content treated as instructions | medium | mitigate | Archived files are written under `.planning/design-archive/` with an index README stating they are a reference archive and are NOT repo code and must not be imported. Fetched bytes are treated as data. |
| T-01.1-13 | Repudiation | Archive silently incomplete (a path missing from the fetch) | low | mitigate | The task's automated verify counts files and asserts the service directory holds exactly 7 entries, so a partial fetch fails the gate rather than passing quietly. |
</threat_model>
